parallel.requirements: The prompt required reading every requirement under /workspace/requirements and implementing all 387, with one non-empty patch per slug and no partial completion.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The agent wrote a 387-node plan and divided remaining work into many child batches across rounds; the final round launched 31 child items for 230 remaining requirements.
parallel.implementation: Parallel produced substantial partial implementation, with 272 requirement patch files collected and five official unit cases passing, but many children remained aborted or incomplete.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery was through shared git commits and requirement_patches files; concurrent shared-tree commits damaged provenance and required reconstructed diffs for some slugs.
parallel.verification: The official direct run-tests.sh failed; results summarized five passed cases and eight failed cases including the pytest tail, so acceptance was not reached.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: At closure, 115 requirements had no collected patch file, 23 final-swarm children were aborted, shared-state conflict/provenance caveats remained, and official status was agent_timeout.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the identical prompt and recognized the 387-requirement scale in its initial reasoning.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Serial kept all work in one main actor, with delegation tools disabled and no subagents or plan artifact recorded.
serial.implementation: Serial only created helper directories and listed requirement titles; no requirement patch files or agent plan were collected.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There was no implemented work to integrate, assemble, or deliver, and the patch timeline stayed empty from start to test.
serial.verification: The official direct run-tests.sh failed and all named unit cases plus the pytest tail failed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The task was essentially unchanged at closure: zero patches, zero plans, no subagents, process_ok false, and failure_mode unknown_agent_error.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had the full prompt requiring every file under /workspace/requirements and produced a 387-node plan before continuing across rounds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the 387-requirement scale in its local reasoning, but did not convert that recognition into patches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the same requirements; parallel attempted broad coverage while serial stopped after setup and requirement-title survey.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the job into child batches, including a final 31-item swarm over 230 remaining requirements with explicit batch ownership notes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial stayed in one main actor with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled and no subagents recorded.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created many concurrent owners and coordination surfaces; serial retained a single local owner but made no deliverable progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included slug batches, scope notes, commit protocol, and cross-batch warnings; returned handoffs also carried caveats about file ownership and conflicts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interfaces or handoff boundaries; it only described a local workflow plan and ran setup commands.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material parallel context issue was not absent task requirements but the shared workspace and commit protocol failing under concurrent ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented many Hadoop changes and the harness collected 272 requirement patch files by the final round.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created local workflow directories and listed requirement titles but the harness collected zero requirement patches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered partial implementation artifacts; serial effectively delivered none.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received an aggregate final swarm result, but it reported 8 completed and 23 aborted children with a resume hint and then cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results, no agent plan, and no patches to retrieve or join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child-result lifecycle at the last fan-out; serial had no child lifecycle at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote a shared repository; one broad commit captured 314 foreign files, later repaired them, and other children reported swept changes and unmerged conflict entries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents or parallel delegation and its patch timeline remained empty.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only the parallel run exposed shared final-tree provenance and merge hazards.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reached official testing after patch collection; run-tests failed, but five named tests passed and eight failed including the pytest tail.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also reached official testing, but all named tests and the pytest tail failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification showed partial functional coverage, whereas serial showed no passing official unit cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed 293,179,520 tokens, hit the official agent timeout, and closed with 272 of 387 patch files collected.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 89,523 tokens, ended with unknown_agent_error rather than timeout, and closed with zero patches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel burned the long-horizon budget on wide concurrent work; serial ended cheaply but without implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both solutions failed. The concrete difference is coverage and process: parallel implemented many requirements and produced 272 patch files but timed out with aborted children and shared-tree provenance damage; serial made no patchable changes and failed every official test. The retained patterns explain adverse parallel process consequences, not a pass/fail outcome split.
parallel_contributors: Partial implementation through multi-agent batches produced 272 patches and five passing official cases.
The final 31-child fan-out over 230 remaining requirements returned 23 aborted children and ended under agent_timeout.
Shared final-tree commits swept other agents work into broad commits, forcing reconstructed diffs and leaving conflict/provenance caveats.
serial_contributors: Serial did not use delegation and did not create an agent plan or requirement patches.
Serial stopped after setup/title-survey behavior and entered official tests with no delivered changes.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel passed five official cases while serial passed none, but both remained far short of the 387-requirement acceptance target.
Many child reports note skipped full builds or environment-limited checks, which are ordinary verification gaps rather than separate concurrency labels.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No discordant outcome; supported contributors explain the different failed trajectories and retained parallel adverse patterns.
